newsitem.title: COMOROS: Campaigning starts for referendum on Comoros.
newsitem.headline: Campaigning starts for referendum on Comoros.

text.p: Campaigning officially started on Sunday for an October 20 referendum on the coup-prone Comoro Islands on a new constitution giving most executive powers to the president.
A presidential decree said campaigning was allowed from Saturday midnight until October 18 under the supervision of a 12-member National Electoral Commission set up for the vote.
The referendum is on a constitution proposed by President Mohamed Taki giving most powers to the presidency ahead of an October 20 election for the federal assembly, disssolved last April.

The Forum of National Recovery, an opposition alliance, is widely expected to call for a boycott of the referendum as opposition parties argue the draft constitution should first be approved by the federal assembly before going to a referendum.

Taki, elected president of the Indian Ocean Islamic republic in March, has banned the sale of alcoholic drinks except to diplomats and foreigners in hotels and has criticised women for wearing mini-skirts.
The Comoros have seen up to 17 coups or attempted coups since independence from France in 1975. In September last year, French forces intervened to quash a coup led by French mercenary Bob Denard.
